title: The Harbor of Port Mahon
premise: In 1756, on the eve of the French siege of Port Mahon, apprentice clockmaker Tamsin Crane is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds the town's requisition ledger hidden in its case—every name, debt, and loyalty recorded by the occupying administration. When British forces retake the harbor, the ledger becomes a weapon: those named as collaborators will hang. Tamsin, who has survived by being invisible, must choose between safety and a peacetime promise made to Élise Vidal, a French clockmaker's daughter now declared enemy, who once saved Tamsin's father from debtor's prison. Keeping the promise means spiriting Élise aboard the last neutral ship before it sails on the morning tide—an act of theft, forgery, and betrayal of the officer who has offered Tasmim protection. The novel ends with the clock striking dawn as the ship slips past the guns; Tamsin stays behind to face the reckoning, carrying only what can be carried, but no longer invisible.
about_author: Felix Joubert is the pen name of a former marine engineer who spent years restoring lighthouse clocks along the Mediterranean coast before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of empire.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Tamsin Crane, apprentice to a dying clockmaker, is summoned to the Governor's observatory to repair the master clock that keeps Port Mahon's time. POV: Tamsin. Beat: quiet competence masking poverty; the first glimpse of how power measures people by their usefulness.

chapters.title: A Ledger in the Case
chapters.summary: Inside the clock's housing Tamsin discovers the occupation ledger—names, debts, denunciations—including their own master's name marked with a black cross. POV: Tamsin. Beat: dread; the realization that time itself has been keeping score.

chapters.title: Élise at the Water Stair
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: three years earlier, Élise Vidal saved Tamsin's father from debtor's prison with a forged receipt, and the two young clockmakers shared one perfect summer before war parted them. POV: Tamsin. Beat: tenderness establishing the promise that will cost everything.

chapters.title: Sails on the Horizon
chapters.summary: British warships appear off the mole; the French garrison begins burning papers, and panic spreads through the lower town. POV: Sergeant Hollis, a weary British officer. Beat: ominous calm before the storm; Hollis is introduced as decent but bound to duty.

chapters.title: The Requisition
chapters.summary: The army seizes the town; soldiers nail requisition notices to doors and demand the ledger be surrendered. Tamsin hides it inside a grandfather clock bound for the chapel loft. POV: Tamsin. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; first act of defiance.

chapters.title: Names Are Currency
chapters.summary: Hollis interrogates townsfolk, offering protection for information; a neighbor denounces the Vidal family as enemy agents still hiding in the wine cellars below the old clock shop. POV: Hollis. Beat: moral unease; he senses the ledger's power and wants it found cleanly.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Tamsin packs their father's tools, the forged-receipt template, and nothing else, learning their master has died overnight—leaving them alone with the secret. POV: Tamsin. Beat: grief compressed into practical motion; survival as discipline.

chapters.title: The Officer's Offer
chapters.summary: Hollis, needing a clockmaker to restore the observatory for gunnery timing, offers Tamsin protection and papers—if they help identify names in the recovered ledger pages. POV: alternating Tamsin and Hollis. Beat: temptation; safety dangled like bait.

chapters.title: Cellar Light
chapters.summary: Tamsin finds Élise alive in the flooded cellar, half-starved, keeping time by counting her own pulse. The promise is renewed aloud: the neutral ship Meridian sails on Thursday's morning tide. POV: Tamsin. Beat: love rekindled under threat; hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Forged in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Using the old receipt template, Tamsin begins forging a neutral-passport for Élise, practicing signatures by lamplight while the town's curfew bells ring wrong. POV: Tamsin. Beat: tension of craft under pressure; every error could mean a rope.

chapters.title: The Black Cross List
chapters.summary: Hollis presents the reconstructed collaborator list to his superiors; Tamsin sees their own name added—not for treason, but because someone denounced them for sheltering 'a Frenchwoman.' POV: Hollis. Beat: horror; duty and justice visibly diverge.

chapters.title: Bells Out of True
chapters.summary: Tamsin deliberately leaves the master clock two minutes slow, buying a small margin of darkness each night, while the garrison blames French saboteurs. POV: Tamsin. Beat: quiet audacity; the clockmaker weaponizes time itself.

chapters.title: An Old Debt Called In
chapters.summary: The harbormaster, whom Tamsin's father once saved, agrees to forge the Meridian's manifest—but demands the ledger page bearing his own compromised name in return. POV: harbormaster Basset. Beat: uneasy alliance; everyone is trading something.

chapters.title: The Informer's Face
chapters.summary: Tamsin discovers the neighbor who denounced Élise is the same man who black-crossed their master—and that he intends to search the chapel loft. POV: Tamsin. Beat: paranoia closing in; the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Fire in the Loft
chapters.summary: Soldiers torch suspected hiding places; the grandfather clock burns, nearly exposing the ledger. Tamsin rescues the pages through smoke, hands scorched, unable to feel the tools afterward. POV: Tamsin. Beat: sacrifice; the body pays for the conscience.

chapters.title: Hollis Suspects
chapters.summary: Hollis notices the clock's deliberate slowness and confronts Tamsin privately, giving them until Friday to confess—because he does not want to believe what the evidence suggests. POV: Hollis. Beat: tragic sympathy; the antagonist as a mirror.

chapters.title: Thursday Night
chapters.summary: Everything converges: forged passport inked, manifest signed, Élise moved by fishing skiff toward the anchored Meridian—while the informer follows and Hollis walks the mole with lantern raised. POV: alternating. Beat: breathless suspense; the plan fraying at every seam.

chapters.title: Two Minutes of Darkness
chapters.summary: Tamsin stops the master clock entirely, plunging the harbor batteries' timing into confusion just as the patrol closes on the skiff; in the unmeasured dark, Élise reaches the ship's ladder. POV: Tamsin. Beat: climax of ingenuity; time given away as a gift.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: At dawn the Meridian slips past the guns on the ebb tide; Élise watches the harbor shrink, holding the broken mainspring Tamsin gave her as a promise kept. POV: Élise. Beat: bittersweet release; love surviving at the cost of separation.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hollis arrests Tamsin at the observatory, where the stopped clock stands as evidence; but the ledger pages Tamsin returns expose the informer's extortions, forcing the commandant to bury the whole affair quietly. POV: Hollis. Beat: justice sideways; corruption devouring its own.

chapters.title: What the Clock Remembers
chapters.summary: Released without charge but stripped of standing, Tamsin repairs the master clock one last time, setting it true, and chooses to stay in Port Mahon rather than flee—keeping the shop, the town, and the memory. POV: Tamsin. Beat: costly integrity; invisibility renounced.

chapters.title: A Letter, Years Later
chapters.summary: Epilogue, 1763: peace declared; a letter arrives from Genoa containing a working pocket watch built from the broken mainspring, set to Port Mahon time, and a single line—'I am counting the days.' POV: Tamsin. Beat: resolution and open horizon; love outlasting empires.
